children: NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL) has secured SJVN’s 265 MW/530 MWh standalone Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in Haryana at a tariff of Rs 2.35 lakh per MW per month.

SJVN acted as the Renewable Energy Implementing Agency (REIA) for the two-hour storage project for Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Limited (UHBVNL). The capacity is divided into two components — 250 MW/500 MWh under Project-1 and 15 MW/30 MWh under Project-2.

The tender was floated in July 2026 and awarded a month later. Other participants included Rama Reflection India, SolarWorld Energy, Pace Digitek, Sun Drop Energia and Oriana Power, which did not make the final list.
Tariff Higher Than Previous Haryana BESS Tender

The discovered tariff of Rs 2.35 lakh per MW per month is higher than the Rs 1.97 lakh per MW per month tariff in an earlier SJVN tender for a 250 MW/500 MWh standalone BESS project at Panipat, Haryana. That project was awarded to Hardi Hydro Energy.

The latest tariff, however, is below those discovered in MSEDCL’s BESS tender, where Oriana Power secured projects at Rs 2.38 lakh and Rs 2.40 lakh per MW per month, while GK Energy secured a project at Rs 2.38 lakh per MW per month.
Under the latest tender, NIRL will provide the BESS to UHBVNL on an on-demand basis to meet peak and off-peak power requirements.
The project is supported by Viability Gap Funding (VGF) of up to Rs 18 lakh per MWh as a one-time, non-recurring expenditure funded through the Power System Development Fund.
Project-2, comprising 15 MW/30 MWh, will receive support under the State Component of the VGF Scheme. Funding has been earmarked for a cumulative 30 MWh of BESS capacity allocated to Haryana.

For this 30 MWh capacity, developers are eligible for VGF of up to Rs 18 lakh per MWh or 30 per cent of the capital cost, as applicable. The grant will be provided as a one-time expenditure and funded through the Central Grant under the State Component of the VGF Scheme.
